hypotheses.root_cause: A routing-dependency deadlock on NOC0 (ring R1, 2 members) that probably involves the PCIE<->DDR path. One transaction, DMA->PCIE txn 0xE470, waits on a circular dependency, never completes and hits the transaction timeout.
hypotheses.rationale:
Causal chain: Dependency cycle forms on ring R1 (3921 ms) -> repeated high txn_q congestion on PCIE<->DDR (stall 28–33%, 3929–4308 ms) as routes on the cycle back up -> the cycle locks up; transactions stuck on it stop moving, so overall fabric telemetry drops to low (stall 1–3%) -> DMA->PCIE txn 0xE470 never completes -> NOC transaction timeout rc=-62 (4738 ms) -> NOC0 error register snapshot -> SYSTEM FATAL interconnect failure (4799 ms). The findings agree on what they rule out, and only one subsystem offers a positive signal.
- PMU: VCORE stable, droop_cnt=0 even at 4771 ms, no gating or DVFS events.
- FW: kept running through the timeout, no exceptions or catalogue markers.
- PCIE: link stayed x4 Gen4 with aer=0, no completion-timeout or credit messages. The retrain rate has been steady since boot, so it isn't the trigger.
- Historian's top matches: QoS starvation (run 000003) and DMA burst overflow (run 000010) both lack their tell-tale lines ('credits=0' / 'burst_len'), so the high similarity scores are probably just because the failure type matches.
- The only catalogue marker present is 'Dependency cycle suspected', 817 ms before the timeout. It is followed by congestion on PCIE<->DDR, the same region the failing DMA->PCIE transaction routes through.
- A quiet fabric at the moment of the timeout argues against starvation, which would show sustained high stall. It fits a localized deadlock, where stuck transactions stop generating traffic.

Why confidence is only moderate:
- There is a single cycle warning, and it says 'suspected'.
- Ring R1's members aren't identified.
- The NOC0 register dump hasn't been decoded.
- We have no DMA-side log, so we can't confirm that 0xE470 was on the cycle or fully rule out a DMA-side cause.
- A PCIE retrain at 4738 ms can't be ruled out, because PCIE logging stops at 4662 ms. (1 of 4 specialists pointed at this cause.)
recommended_actions: Decode the NOC0 register snapshot (20 words, 0x60000E59–0x60000EA5) against the fabric register map: per-port outstanding counts, credit counters, arbiter state, and which ports/VCs are blocked, to confirm a circular wait involving the DMA->PCIE route.

Identify the two members of ring R1 from the route tables or the fabric configuration, and check whether the DMA->PCIE and PCIE<->DDR paths share virtual channels or buffers that could create a cyclic dependency.

Rerun with NoC deadlock-detection or trace enabled (transaction trace on NOC0 from 3900 ms) and with DMA logging enabled (descriptors and burst_len for 0xE470), to rule out a DMA burst overflow that the logs can't see.
Reproduce with separate VC/escape-channel assignment for DMA->PCIE vs PCIE->DDR traffic, or with the cycle-forming route disabled; if timeouts disappear, deadlock is confirmed.

Increase PCIE logging granularity around the failure window, and correlate retrain timestamps with the timeout, to rule out a PCIE retrain at 4738 ms stalling the target; separately investigate the steady ~10/s retrain rate as a link-quality issue.

trace.note: The failure is a NoC timeout on a DMA-to-PCIE transaction. The two closest past incidents point to NoC QoS starvation and DMA burst overflow, so the NOC specialist should decode the register dump to tell these apart. PCIE is the destination, and an unresponsive endpoint is a likely upstream cause. PMU covers power or clock transitions that could stall the fabric. FW covers how the DMA and QoS were configured. BOOT, DDR, and THERMAL are lower priority: the path doesn't involve DDR, and there's no thermal signal in the error lines.
